evidence.excerpt: Critical infrastructure sectors—including energy, water, transportation, and telecommunications—face an evolving and increasingly sophisticated threat landscape. Numerous cybersecurity frameworks have been developed to guide operators in assessing and improving their security posture, including NIST CSF, IEC 62443, NERC CIP, and ISA/IEC standards. Despite their widespread adoption, significant gaps remain in how these frameworks address emerging challenges such as cloud-connected OT environments, AI-driven attacks, and supply chain interdependencies. This survey systematically reviews twelve major cybersecurity frameworks applicable to critical infrastructure, evaluating them across dimensions of scope, implementation guidance, assessment methodology, and adaptability to ICS-specific threats. A structured gap analysis reveals that most frameworks inadequately address real-time anomaly detection requirements, provide insufficient guidance on IoT integration, and lack concrete metrics for evaluating detection and response effectiveness. The paper proposes a consolidated gap taxonomy and outlines a research agenda addressing the most critical deficiencies. It is intended as a reference for both practitioners implementing security programmes and researchers developing next-generation framework components.
